body:
Three states are about to decide a lot more than 2026.

| | | |
---
Peter,
---
We've looked at the polling in every swing state and swing race in the country. It's margin of error, either way, almost everywhere.

At this point, it's not about winning anybody over. _It's about who actually shows up._

If conservatives turn out in November, we'll win every critical battleground and lay the groundwork for victory in 2028 and beyond.

That's why Turning Point Action is focusing all our efforts on three key states: Arizona, Nevada, and New Hampshire.

**We call these states the new RED WALL.**

_Let me explain why they matter so much... _

After 2024, Charlie looked at the numbers, looked at the maps, and told our team something simple. If we lock down Arizona, Nevada, and New Hampshire, the Left's entire strategy falls apart. Their map collapses. Their path back to power disappears.

Here's why... Winning the presidency comes down to 270 electoral votes. Lose Arizona and most of the realistic paths to the White House in 2028 are gone. Lose Nevada and New Hampshire and the Left rebuilds the Blue Wall they lost in 2024.

Whoever wins in 2028 controls the 2030 Census. The Census drives redistricting. Redistricting sets the congressional map for the next ten years.

This midterm decides which way that goes.

name: Abdul
subject: “You can’t”
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Abdul for U
body:
Peter, for years, the people who write the biggest checks in our politics told us the same thing: _you can't._
You _can't_ run a campaign without taking corporate PAC money.
You _can't_ say out loud that this seat isn't for sale and expect to still be standing at the end of it.
You _can't_ win in Michigan without making a few concessions to your values.
They said our movement wouldn’t make it through the primary. We faced $70 million in outside spending. It was one of the most expensive Democratic primaries in American history.
You know what happened next: **we WON** — and not by accident.
We won because nurses and autoworkers and volunteers knocked doors and sent us five and ten bucks at a time, and it added up to something the big money interests couldn't buy.
We defied the status quo once, and now we have to do it again.
* **September 30, this Wednesday, marks our final FEC quarterly deadline before Election Day.** After that, everything we've raised and spent gets reported out publicly.

* **Mike Rogers will read our report. So will Donald Trump, Elon Musk, and the MAGA billionaire donors bankrolling Rogers’ campaign.** They’ll take a look at our numbers to decide how much more cash they should dump into Michigan.

* **The stronger we look, the more nervous they’ll get.** They won’t want to risk wasting a bunch of money here if it looks like Rogers is a lost cause.

So that’s our goal: **raise as much as we possibly can before the month is over to ward off any future GOP investments.**
I don’t take corporate PAC money. I never have, and I never will. So even though I don’t love asking for money, I have to. It’s the only way we can defy the odds again and win this November:
[_**https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-ms-aes-20260928-5-ak**_](https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20260928-5-ak.klqPWw&amount=5&refcode=em20260928-3333&t=2&akid=3333%2E251025%2ErEb81S)
Thank you, thank you, thank you. We truly could not do this without you, Peter. 🙏
Your friend in the fight,
Abdul

body:
There has been a lot of discussion as to what I plan to do in 2028...

[](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/kdh-fftp-em?refcode=em260928&refcode2=1367_2563979_-NdH0O&akid=1367%2E2563979%2E-NdH0O)
---
Peter -
There has been a lot of discussion as to what I plan to do in 2028. I can understand why so many people would like to jump ahead to the end of this chaotic and cruel administration.
So here's the truth:
I am completely focused on the midterm elections. To be quite serious about it, 2028 does not matter if we do not win in 2026.
Let me tell you something, Peter: The midterm elections are one of the only ways that we can put a check on this administration in the immediate future.
If we do not stop them now, Donald Trump and his enablers will continue to steal the power of the people for their own benefit. Think of all they have done in just the past two years, and how much we can prevent in the future by acting now.
The outcome of these races are going to affect so much in terms of our access to affordable and quality health care, childcare, housing, and more.
That is why I am so focused on investing in candidates now so we can overwhelmingly elect leaders this November who will fight for us.
Just this month, I campaigned with Dr. Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan and announced my plans to get out the vote with Sen. Jon Ossoff in Georgia, because I know their races impact voters across our entire county. The U.S. Senate should be a stopgap on the abuses of this administration, and these leaders will fulfill that duty — if we ensure they are elected.
This is what I am doing next with Fight for The People PAC. I am traveling, speaking out, and helping elect Democrats everywhere before the midterms — and I cannot do this alone.
I am counting on your donations to fuel this important work. We have our last FEC report of this midterm election coming up soon on Wednesday, where we're legally required to report what we've raised. I can assure you, everyone will be looking to see what we report.
**[If you are still with me, I am asking you to make a contribution of $5 or any amount you can afford to get us started. Do it before our FEC deadline. It would mean a lot to me.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/kdh-fftp-em?refcode=em260928&refcode2=1367_2563979_-NdH0O&akid=1367%2E2563979%2E-NdH0O)

body:

Hi, it’s
Jocelyn.

I hate to be so direct, but our last end-of-quarter deadline is in two
days, and I could use your help. [ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/19218?t=1002&akid=1927%2E181023%2E0SxoYq ]I’m humbly asking if you will make your
first contribution to our campaign before our end-of-quarter
deadline.

ballots are now available across Michigan.

dismantle our right to vote by mail, millions of Michiganders vote by mail
every election.

Detroit, now.

body:
| | | | | | | Friends,

When I was a deputy prosecutor in Spokane, the first question in almost every case was the simplest one: what benefits The People?
Now as a candidate to represent Eastern Washington in Congress, I have been asking that all week.
Michael Baumgartner was a pivotal vote for the **One Big Beautiful Bill** – Donald Trump said so himself on Monday. That bill has **added $4 trillion to our national debt–so far.** It **cuts Medicaid, the program our rural critical access hospitals depend on**. Hospital leaders in this district have told me they could be "smothered to death in five to seven years" without that funding.
**Does that benefit The People?**
Not the families in Dayton or Colville or Clarkston who would drive an hour to the next closest ER. The people who benefit are the ones writing the checks: corporate PACs, GOP leadership, and the outsiders lining up behind the President's endorsement.
After leaving the prosecutor’s office I spent 24 years representing our country, and I was just as clear about who I worked for. I worked for the American people.
**In Congress, I will work for Eastern Washington, and the only people I will owe anything to are right here at home. That’s why I don’t take corporate PAC money, and it’s why this deadline matters so much. Every contribution on my report represents a real person.**
**We have 2 days left. Please chip in whatever you can to ensure that all of us in Eastern Washington benefit from this election.**

clean_body: | Fellow Republican, I understand that you get spammed with a whole lot of emails and texts from Republicans, especially in these final weeks of the midterms, so I try to avoid sending them whenever possible. Well, this might just be the single most important message I've ever written! But because of that, I'm under pressure to make every word count - and honestly, it's really hard to find the right words to convey the scale of the threat facing America. At this point, I've re-written this letter several times, and ultimately, I decided to just write to you straight from my heart with words inspired by my unwavering faith in God and our Country. There are no media consultants or comms people changing my words or watering down my thoughts. This all comes straight from , so I apologize if it's a bit rough around the edges. I'm not repeating the same worn-out talking points you're probably used to! Look - I know the mainstream media is downplaying it, but the Democrat Party is getting more and more extreme, to the point that I believe they pose a threat to our free Republic. They're embracing Communists, pro-Sharia candidates, and all kinds of radical Leftists who HATE conservatives, Christians, and the very values that made our country great. There was a time not too long ago when American voters would punish this kind of extremism at the ballot box. But instead, polling shows the Democrats are SURGING to their largest ever lead - - in the final weeks of the election! How are they winning in the polls? It's certainly not because American voters suddenly support radical ideas like communism, open borders, and defunding the police. A lot of elected officials aren't willing to say this, but I will... The left hates you, they hate your vote, and they hate MAGA for putting America First! Right now, they're spending to fully verify that new electorate to ensure that every last Democrat voter (illegals too!) casts a ballot in November. At the end of the day, winning the midterms is a simple numbers game, and as it stands, the American people still have the upper hand on the Left. 2024 proved that decisively! But our advantage disappears the second Republicans stop showing up to vote... We need to verify that every Republican voter - especially - will show up to cast a ballot on or before November 3rd. If Republicans don't turn out and we LOSE the midterms, the consequences for our country will be downright catastrophic. The America we fought so hard to SAVE in 2024 will crumble before our very eyes! That's why I'm appealing to you personally... | Thank you, Rep. Peter,
**While Big Pharma and insurance companies are raking in record profits, the Trump administration and Republicans in Congress are sitting back letting working people pay the price.**
Every month, lifesaving medicine costs more.
Every week, more claims for essential care get denied.
Every single time, working people pay the price.
At the same time, Trump and his MAGA allies are gutting Medicaid, the lifeline that millions of poor and working families count on for health coverage.
**Make no mistake: this is a choice.**
Drug companies could cap their prices. Insurance companies could cover the care people are already paying for. Republicans could expand Medicaid. _They’re choosing not to because they’ve chosen profits over people_.
I’ve been fighting for Medicare For All my entire career. I’ve introduced the bill in the House every single session. And I’m not stopping until we get it done, because healthcare is a human right and the status quo is failing too many people.
But I can’t pass Medicare For All alone. I need fighters in Congress who aren’t afraid to take on Trump, stand up to corporate power, and put working people first.

| | | |

[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140176990/649809118/2110272206?amount=25&refcode=260928em_rb_sjw&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MTI2MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhNWMwNTg2My1hN2JiLWYxMTEtYTZhOS0wMDBkM2E1NmQyZjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=2eWYY63BZHS00VC2k3DqsCN_ZVL7UqaF3M04L6VR9JA=)

I want to share a bit about my personal life that you may not know yet. I was raised by social justice warriors. My dad marched for civil rights in Selma, Alabama, where he heard Martin Luther King Jr. preach. My mom, born and raised in the Philippines, spent years fighting for the restoration of democracy in her home country. They had me while living and working in the Philippines as social justice missionaries. I was born when a dictator was rising to power and martial law was imminent. It was critical to both of my parents that I grow up in a country with democracy, freedom, rule of law, and human and civil rights — and sadly it became clear to them that wasn’t the case in the Philippines. So they brought my family here, to California, when I was just two months old.
---
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140176991/649809119/2110272206?amount=25&refcode=260928em_rb_sjw&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MTI2MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhNWMwNTg2My1hN2JiLWYxMTEtYTZhOS0wMDBkM2E1NmQyZjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=2eWYY63BZHS00VC2k3DqsCN_ZVL7UqaF3M04L6VR9JA=)
---
A short while later, my parents began working with the United Farm Workers of America — fighting for workers’ rights, fair pay, and shade and water breaks alongside Dolores Huerta and Philip Vera Cruz. I would never have guessed as a young kid that I would grow up to serve as the Attorney General of California — but as long as I can remember, I’ve known that I wanted to fight for those most vulnerable to have a fair shot at the California Dream. That’s why I do this work. I know, without a doubt, that the California Dream is alive and well because I’m living mine — and I’m committed to using every bit of platform and power I have to lift people up and fight for justice for all. _I’m on the ballot for re-election in just 36 days, and I want nothing more than to continue this fight._ **California needs an Attorney General who will stand up to those who abuse their power** — whether it’s corrupt politicians, corporate polluters, extremist groups trying to roll back our rights, or powerful interests that exploit workers, cheat consumers, and put profits ahead of people. **[We have an important end-of-quarter deadline this Wednesday at midnight, and every single dollar we raise before then will make an impact on what we can do — in my re-election campaign, and in our movement to secure justice and accountability for all. It was critical to both of my parents that I grow up in a country with democracy, freedom, rule of law, and human and civil rights — and sadly it became clear to them that wasn’t the case in the Philippines. As one of the most engaged supporters of my U.S. Senate campaign in North Carolina, you have made a deep impact on our ability to stay in this fight. Thank you.
I hope you know how much I appreciate your time and attention – [**_and today, I’m asking you to take the next step and make a donation of $5._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1451&amount=5&t=8&akid=4000%2E124072%2EB7B94r) Here’s why:
**Our final FEC end-of-quarter deadline before the election is in just four days – and we’re falling short of our goal. The timing is less than ideal.**
The GOP (including President Trump’s super PAC) is spending more than $100 million to defeat me. Trump and JD Vance just came to North Carolina to rally for my opponent and call on outside spending groups to dump even more dark money into this race. Far-right super PACs are spreading lies about me and completely distorting my record.
Now, their attacks are working: A recent poll shows my slim lead cut to a statistical tie.

**********OSSINING, NY –** Army combat veteran and Democratic nominee Cait Conley faced off against Rep. From exposing party-first politician Mike Lawler’s [100% voting record with Donald Trump](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.fYwBmNOg9T7TSqRCKjNSzXtCMKHcN2ul7HRUCTRtim9lVk78sRcbBuzd4S79Yg_FbHrBy1l9SMd3z0gRc2THLVtWsmT0JStEqPdHesKQewKqNBmHnNjav0TZHeKv23Q-sMyEZkJCakNXgVzAF9H7cukTIQB-MYEGUKXmD6HwziDzN_xg4zra4CgG5THRwNTOTaoi6V4O8n-0qw6e_rkNqhU3Y5ZT9nBJyhZnw3wL8RUujGMg9hOr0j9oppE2LlEEeU0YDMi9TkFkMvshc63Ai94CMKcWjLCLs1_MaJzR_IytfqWlxEPJhit4IzFAcXiJBQ4SdVo9kNBzrpMWwdZWY5eAIO0Jey6FAEpB7tEF45jfZSe2VscqPGz-ZkUiuHzd/4ug/5ACKNsLQSbu8CktFviy35g/h0/h001.N-ml5PB0ubOI-nH3u6r0V3KW6RZkugccDWRxlH1Jvog) and its harmful impacts on the Hudson Valley to being the only candidate on the stage with a clear plan to rein in Washington corruption and lower costs for working families, Cait Conley cemented herself as the future leader NY-17 needs and deserves. **Cait Conley spokesperson Maddy Rosen:** _“The contrast between Cait Conley and Mike Lawler has never been clearer than it was on the debate stage tonight. body:
| | | 7 Directions of Service Newsletter: September 2026 Sep 28, 2026
## A Letter from Our Co-Founders
Dear friends, As September comes to a close, one question keeps coming up in everything we do: **who pays?** Who pays when data centers need more power and families see it on their electric bills? Who pays when pipelines cross our rivers and sacred places? Who pays when laws that protect our water, our homelands, and our right to go to court are weakened behind closed doors? And who is left standing alone when funders get scared and walk away? This month, we carried that question everywhere we went. In August, 250 of you filled the Varsity Theatre in Chapel Hill for two nights of VS. GOLIATH, and 45 of you stepped up to take action. In September, we brought Tuscarora and Lumbee voices from North Carolina to NYC Climate Week, into rooms where frontline communities are too often missing. And here at home, we kept watch as Section 106 protections for sacred sites and a secret "permitting reform" deal threatened the tools our communities depend on. In this issue, you'll find stories from the frontlines, updates on the fights ahead, and ways to get involved, from our Community Pipeline Safety Meeting this Wednesday in Mebane to a quiet afternoon of rest with the Thunderhorse herd in October. Because this work takes courage, and it also takes care. We live on the same earth, breathe the same air, and drink the same water. What affects one of us will eventually affect all of us. Thank you for standing with us. In community and gratitude, C&J;

## VS. GOLIATH: 250 People, Two Nights, One Shared Struggle
On August 26 and 27, 7 Directions of Service welcomed 250 people to the Varsity Theatre in Chapel Hill for two nights of documentary film, conversation, and community action: 100 people the first night and 150 the second. Night One: Appalachia and Cancer Alley. We opened the evening with a powerful spoken word performance by 7DS Poet Laureate LJ Bowens. The films took us to Appalachia and Louisiana's Cancer Alley, where communities have lived for generations with extraction, fossil fuel infrastructure, and industrial pollution. After the screening, Russell Chisholm of POWHR and landowner Maury Johnson, who traveled from Virginia and West Virginia to be with us, joined documentarian and film producer Sam Eilertsen and Jason Keck of 7DS for a panel sharing firsthand stories from the fight against the Mountain Valley Pipeline. Night Two: Greater Chaco and Port Arthur The second night traveled west to the Greater Chaco region and south to Port Arthur, Texas. Diné leaders Mario Atencio and Daniel Tso joined documentarian and film producer Maggie Lemere for a conversation about Indigenous sovereignty, sacred places, and what happens when homelands are treated as resources to be extracted. We closed the night with words on environmental justice from our American Indian youth, Mr. and Miss NC NAYO 2026, a reminder that the next generation is already carrying this work forward. From Watching to Action Each night, we connected these national stories to the fights happening right here in North Carolina, from pipelines crossing our rivers to threats to sacred places and ancestral landscapes. By the end of the two nights, 45 people had signed up to take action to protect their communities. Thank You To everyone who filled the theater: thank you for showing up. And thank you to our sponsors, who made it possible to offer free popcorn and beverages to every viewer, keeping the event welcoming and accessible to all. Together, we moved from watching to witnessing, and from witnessing to action.

## Who Pays for Power? 7DS Takes North Carolina's Frontlines to NYC Climate Week
The traffic stopped. Police lined the intersections, and President Trump's 85-car motorcade rolled through Manhattan while everyone else waited. It was a fitting welcome to a week when Climate Week and the UN General Assembly turned New York into a stage for power: who holds it, who moves freely, and who is told to wait. We came to ask one question: **Who pays for power?** In Midtown Manhattan's Fashion District, 7DS hosted a hybrid gathering that carried North Carolina's Tribal and frontline voices into the heart of Climate Week. Joining from home were **Ramona BigEagle** (Tuscarora), **Eudora Hunt** (council leader, Tuscarora Nation of North Carolina), and **Donnie Locklear** (Lumbee, retired Navy veteran), with 7DS's **Seth Harris** and **Jason Keck** in the room. While other rooms talked about innovation and investment, ours talked about the real cost: rising utility bills, new gas plants and pipelines driven by data centers and AI, and rivers and sacred places standing in the path. **The motorcades have left the city. The work continues here at home.** [Read the full story] | [Take Action](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm38fvtAI0s2k031ncLENvJQyuGBRQCgAcYIRuI-COuuPdi2dM0uG1XpDX7vyjGwliHRjdDS4g6qobAZK8UGdLNTjS8WgKNzOxlf6mcoGGMpf0fgyI7vVupu_6oAS-07BTTyAJwV__Dwwrcrdr-S6153aknn3g1giv_BpkxGcKn7Ov_Wc3wB-ci1j-_pO3PgCpXVLzOlqtLxckd47k3hCLaS2-NQHSkQGhPRzzJuOvjPf0z4lcv5yIGzMy7sIdsJ2ESWPs9PDtAKmEJMNm0sFUdW6zhJkHu30fA9wwA2awQ21VWoYG8gy0G2U7APajUL55f1G4ppgk3SOZ4dya__xo5cTXkKslKHQiLl-DUS4HNh8mw/4ug/1J4GsvP6TN6pDUYGWsI-8Q/h0/h001.w3JGbNI_ULOSdZbt35bE01tQcxS4V0-LKYwhoKEofhU)

## Decided in the Dark: The Secret "Permitting Reform" Deal
It keeps happening the same way. On Monday, September 28, we heard that Senate Majority Leader Thune might move for cloture on a deregulatory "permitting reform" deal. The text hadn't been released. As far as we could tell, it hadn't even been finalized. Senators were being asked to advance a bill no one had been allowed to read. This is how decisions about our land and water keep getting made: behind closed doors, on rushed timelines, with the people who have to live with the consequences finding out last. Large environmental organizations get their own briefings. Frontline communities and Tribal Nations are left in the dark. By the time the public sees what's in the deal, it's already too late to change it. And what we are hearing about this framework is alarming. It could:
* Severely restrict judicial review, closing the courthouse door to the communities most harmed
* Gut NEPA's environmental review and public input
* Weaken the Endangered Species Act
* Limit the National Historic Preservation Act and Tribal and community consultation over sacred and historic sites
* Undermine the Clean Water Act's protections for rivers, wetlands, and drinking water

Notice the pattern. The very laws that let communities see what's coming, ask questions, and speak up are the ones being weakened. A deal made in the dark that takes away the public's right to be heard. This is not reform. **This is deregulation.** It hands the fossil fuel industry a giveaway, lets Big Tech and data center developers build energy-hungry AI facilities faster and with less scrutiny, and leaves frontline communities, Tribal Nations, and fenceline neighbors to pay the price. A bill that is good for the public does not need to be rushed through in the dark. **Make your voice heard.** Call the Capitol Switchboard at **(202) 224-3121** and ask for Senator Tillis and Senator Budd. Tell them: **"Vote NO on any permitting deal that hasn't been made public. No secret deals."** Read why we're sounding the alarm: [This Is Deregulation. Environmental Racism Is Happening Today.](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.VaNbvq2kCafTMdHbdpp0pvxUCYOjVkcJ_F94NuUPwrT6s3lyV8AYR6du0ds9V93_RwElGbIKl8LCfl6wR53G9R5WZFN9XWaPxAN2FzLHkfqNj2F0bQzmP8vNY021DLIPxHT0FO4TO-mwaKhSknPWCoELL15s_6COZ2lrZHoP7Wgyn4zM_dBR-P4_LnJDOYuT1-I2EUMrZzFQ8M7PbxjMzuCrLE-oofYbMRQlJrXZqKrFGSfRog6EK0VNO20AKDVUHNYA8UJh_pHR-_lFGKekcusuAKwzIToS5RwYk43xvjWLEEz5kaST-nIQEFFL56PoIQPnsqtczBa6BgvW0Xa5WlTyYMyEGh9xOzu70JyZR81vIfwOfjnL4N8_cy7VU8UW-upU3a5CpM3BYpJWER3abs82CFmIYr_9G1gUpaeUb7I/4ug/1J4GsvP6TN6pDUYGWsI-8Q/h1/h001.0K2CTN_NNMB-mIDuTl1mPG1jT4cPhMRoXyCZMOeJBvI)
## Section 106 Is Under Review. Tribal Voices Need to Be Heard.
The Advisory Council on Historic Preservation has proposed changes to Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act. Section 106 is one of the few tools Tribal Nations have to require federal agencies to stop, consult, and consider the impacts of their projects on sacred places, burial grounds, and cultural landscapes before it's too late. Before any agency can move forward with a significant new rule, it must go through review by the White House Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs (OIRA) under Executive Order 12866. That review is an opportunity: Tribal leaders, Tribal Historic Preservation Officers, and others can request a meeting with OIRA and speak directly about how these changes would affect their communities. The process is simple and can be done online. A sacred place does not stop being sacred because a regulation changed. ## Who Pays for North Carolina's AI Energy Boom?
Duke Energy Progress says its fuel charge is going down. But that's not the whole bill. When all of the proposed rider changes before the North Carolina Utilities Commission are combined, Duke estimates that a household using 1,000 kilowatt-hours a month would pay about **$3.61 more every month** , a 2.1 percent increase. A headline saying "fuel costs are going down" doesn't mean your bill is. And this is happening as AI and hyperscale data centers drive extraordinary new electricity demand in North Carolina. Artificial intelligence may feel "virtual," but the infrastructure behind it is very physical: substations, transmission lines, gas plants, pipelines, and water. Duke's fuel costs include not only the fuel itself but the cost of _transporting_ it, at the same moment our state is debating new gas generation and major pipelines. So we're asking the questions regulators should answer before these costs become embedded in people's bills:
* Who pays for the transmission upgrades and new generation?
* Who pays to transport the fuel?
* Who carries the risk if data center demand never materializes?
* And who bears the environmental and cultural costs when that infrastructure crosses rural, Black, and Indigenous communities?

**Rural families cannot become the subsidy for the AI economy.** _Read the full post:_[_Who Pays for North Carolina's AI Energy Boom?_](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.VaNbvq2kCafTMdHbdpp0pvxUCYOjVkcJ_F94NuUPwrSv1Vmhgmy_Ed20Oz6fbzdE32iUfGBWYxTRXih7zPYB8a6qEWn7UnJpT8EbYFpBOaHxYjBdGlolvt4A7KTZOBotaBrmvhUdRnprKJzyOdgFIq1V7pfGRr854sijraPszHoAOL3bHPE2YGvcZKzcZiYoOQVLxwgPLhX-NmAFl3-z8ZWbuhDXDnmIvKeWzcNDZurQ6fK8vWzYFILIZQsdU6pUOLP4epIS_zEyZxXi5JVuvsfoMoYl-j9A1B26dFgVqz2Lswah3skS_I3m5CoVhFOzZ_fTddPcMVDzphsNedVbymxqWYWC8LSLAU2LxgmNvja3xEiEZK2q6NZLQw-c7-Iv1ya-4easBLUl5gZa15izgrBkWjq9fttkx8KWkv4oNMs/4ug/1J4GsvP6TN6pDUYGWsI-8Q/h6/h001.NaJHWB6AwDMEsL5NqG-ViVglprvtlf2VnvGXLMpSyoY)

## Volunteers Needed: Community Pipeline Watch
Three major natural gas projects, the **Southeast Supply Enhancement Project (SSEP)** , **MVP Southgate** , and the **T-15 Reliability Project** , are moving through communities across North Carolina. 7 Directions of Service is expanding our community-led construction, water, and air monitoring, and **we need you.** Permits have requirements. Construction has conditions. Environmental protections only work when someone is paying attention to whether they are being followed. That's where community monitoring comes in. **You don't have to be a scientist, attorney, or environmental professional.** Training and guidance will be provided. Choose the area that fits you:
* **Construction Watch:** Observe construction from lawful public locations and document erosion, sediment, or stormwater concerns
* **Water Watch:** Monitor streams, creeks, and wetlands near construction areas
* **Air Watch:** Help with community air monitoring and maintain equipment
* **Research & Compliance:** Review public NCDEQ and FERC records for inspections, incidents, and enforcement
* **Mapping & Data:** Organize photos, locations, and records to spot patterns across all three projects
* **Community Outreach:** Help residents learn how to document and report concerns

Your safety comes first. Volunteers will **never** be asked to trespass, enter construction zones, confront workers, or put themselves in unsafe situations. ## Dear Funders: Now Is Not the Time to Be Scared
A few years ago, funders were showing up for frontline communities all across Turtle Island. Then Trump was elected, and almost immediately, funders panicked. We were even invited to an event where frontline leaders asked funders not to be afraid and to keep investing in the frontline. But as soon as the buffoons in charge started making threats, many of the people who felt uncomfortable pulled back. Some went across the pond to fund other fights. That left many frontline communities alone, without the resources to defend themselves. **We don't have that option.** Many of us work two and three jobs to make ends meet, and we still do what we have to do to protect our communities. clean_body: | | | 7 Directions of Service Newsletter: September 2026 Sep 28, 2026 A Letter from Our Co-Founders Dear friends, As September comes to a close, one question keeps coming up in everything we do: who pays? Who pays when data centers need more power and families see it on their electric bills? Who pays when pipelines cross our rivers and sacred places? Who pays when laws that protect our water, our homelands, and our right to go to court are weakened behind closed doors? And who is left standing alone when funders get scared and walk away? This month, we carried that question everywhere we went. In August, 250 of you filled the Varsity Theatre in Chapel Hill for two nights of VS. GOLIATH, and 45 of you stepped up to take action. In September, we brought Tuscarora and Lumbee voices from North Carolina to NYC Climate Week, into rooms where frontline communities are too often missing. And here at home, we kept watch as Section 106 protections for sacred sites and a secret "permitting reform" deal threatened the tools our communities depend on. In this issue, you'll find stories from the frontlines, updates on the fights ahead, and ways to get involved, from our Community Pipeline Safety Meeting this Wednesday in Mebane to a quiet afternoon of rest with the Thunderhorse herd in October. Because this work takes courage, and it also takes care. We live on the same earth, breathe the same air, and drink the same water. What affects one of us will eventually affect all of us. Thank you for standing with us. In community and gratitude, C&J; VS. GOLIATH: 250 People, Two Nights, One Shared Struggle On August 26 and 27, 7 Directions of Service welcomed 250 people to the Varsity Theatre in Chapel Hill for two nights of documentary film, conversation, and community action: 100 people the first night and 150 the second. Night One: Appalachia and Cancer Alley. We opened the evening with a powerful spoken word performance by 7DS Poet Laureate LJ Bowens. The films took us to Appalachia and Louisiana's Cancer Alley, where communities have lived for generations with extraction, fossil fuel infrastructure, and industrial pollution. After the screening, Russell Chisholm of POWHR and landowner Maury Johnson, who traveled from Virginia and West Virginia to be with us, joined documentarian and film producer Sam Eilertsen and Jason Keck of 7DS for a panel sharing firsthand stories from the fight against the Mountain Valley Pipeline. Night Two: Greater Chaco and Port Arthur The second night traveled west to the Greater Chaco region and south to Port Arthur, Texas. Diné leaders Mario Atencio and Daniel Tso joined documentarian and film producer Maggie Lemere for a conversation about Indigenous sovereignty, sacred places, and what happens when homelands are treated as resources to be extracted. We closed the night with words on environmental justice from our American Indian youth, Mr. and Miss NC NAYO 2026, a reminder that the next generation is already carrying this work forward. From Watching to Action Each night, we connected these national stories to the fights happening right here in North Carolina, from pipelines crossing our rivers to threats to sacred places and ancestral landscapes. By the end of the two nights, 45 people had signed up to take action to protect their communities. Thank You To everyone who filled the theater: thank you for showing up. And thank you to our sponsors, who made it possible to offer free popcorn and beverages to every viewer, keeping the event welcoming and accessible to all. Together, we moved from watching to witnessing, and from witnessing to action. Who Pays for Power? 7DS Takes North Carolina's Frontlines to NYC Climate Week The traffic stopped. Police lined the intersections, and President Trump's 85-car motorcade rolled through Manhattan while everyone else waited. It was a fitting welcome to a week when Climate Week and the UN General Assembly turned New York into a stage for power: who holds it, who moves freely, and who is told to wait. We came to ask one question: Who pays for power? In Midtown Manhattan's Fashion District, 7DS hosted a hybrid gathering that carried North Carolina's Tribal and frontline voices into the heart of Climate Week. Joining from home were Ramona BigEagle (Tuscarora), Eudora Hunt (council leader, Tuscarora Nation of North Carolina), and Donnie Locklear (Lumbee, retired Navy veteran), with 7DS's Seth Harris and Jason Keck in the room. While other rooms talked about innovation and investment, ours talked about the real cost: rising utility bills, new gas plants and pipelines driven by data centers and AI, and rivers and sacred places standing in the path. The motorcades have left the city. The work continues here at home. [Read the full story] | Decided in the Dark: The Secret "Permitting Reform" Deal It keeps happening the same way. On Monday, September 28, we heard that Senate Majority Leader Thune might move for cloture on a deregulatory "permitting reform" deal. The text hadn't been released. As far as we could tell, it hadn't even been finalized. Senators were being asked to advance a bill no one had been allowed to read. This is how decisions about our land and water keep getting made: behind closed doors, on rushed timelines, with the people who have to live with the consequences finding out last. Large environmental organizations get their own briefings. Frontline communities and Tribal Nations are left in the dark. By the time the public sees what's in the deal, it's already too late to change it. And what we are hearing about this framework is alarming. It could: Severely restrict judicial review, closing the courthouse door to the communities most harmed Gut NEPA's environmental review and public input Weaken the Endangered Species Act Limit the National Historic Preservation Act and Tribal and community consultation over sacred and historic sites Undermine the Clean Water Act's protections for rivers, wetlands, and drinking water Notice the pattern. The very laws that let communities see what's coming, ask questions, and speak up are the ones being weakened. A deal made in the dark that takes away the public's right to be heard. This is not reform. This is deregulation. It hands the fossil fuel industry a giveaway, lets Big Tech and data center developers build energy-hungry AI facilities faster and with less scrutiny, and leaves frontline communities, Tribal Nations, and fenceline neighbors to pay the price. A bill that is good for the public does not need to be rushed through in the dark. Make your voice heard. Call the Capitol Switchboard at (202) 224-3121 and ask for Senator Tillis and Senator Budd. Tell them: "Vote NO on any permitting deal that hasn't been made public. No secret deals." Read why we're sounding the alarm: Section 106 Is Under Review. Tribal Voices Need to Be Heard. The Advisory Council on Historic Preservation has proposed changes to Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act. Section 106 is one of the few tools Tribal Nations have to require federal agencies to stop, consult, and consider the impacts of their projects on sacred places, burial grounds, and cultural landscapes before it's too late. Before any agency can move forward with a significant new rule, it must go through review by the White House Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs (OIRA) under Executive Order 12866. That review is an opportunity: Tribal leaders, Tribal Historic Preservation Officers, and others can request a meeting with OIRA and speak directly about how these changes would affect their communities. The process is simple and can be done online. A sacred place does not stop being sacred because a regulation changed. Once a site is destroyed, it cannot be put back. Read why 7 Directions of Service is sounding the alarm: Rights of Nature: What If the Water Itself Had Rights? Our laws treat rivers as property. When a river is poisoned, the courts ask whether a permit was broken, not whether the river herself was harmed. For Indigenous peoples, the water has always been a relative, not a resource. 7 Directions of Service co-authored North Carolina's Rights of Nature legislation for the Haw and Dan Rivers, and we are working with Tribal Nations to recognize the rights of the waters they have loved the longest. Read the full post: Learn the Rights of Nature with Dr. Crystal What would it mean if rivers, forests, and wetlands had the legal right to exist, flourish, and heal? Around the world, communities and Tribal Nations are already answering that question, and now you can learn how. Introduction to Rights of Nature is a self-paced online course taught by 7DS Executive Director Dr. Crystal Cavalier-Keck , co-author of North Carolina's Rights of Nature river legislation. 6 modules , self-paced, start anytime $75 for lifetime access Financial assistance available on request. Email mailto:info@7directionsofservice.com Whether you're an organizer, student, educator, Tribal leader, or simply someone who loves a river, this course will give you the tools to understand and advocate for the rights of the natural world. | Who Pays for North Carolina's AI Energy Boom? Duke Energy Progress says its fuel charge is going down. But that's not the whole bill. When all of the proposed rider changes before the North Carolina Utilities Commission are combined, Duke estimates that a household using 1,000 kilowatt-hours a month would pay about $3.61 more every month , a 2.1 percent increase. A headline saying "fuel costs are going down" doesn't mean your bill is. And this is happening as AI and hyperscale data centers drive extraordinary new electricity demand in North Carolina. Artificial intelligence may feel "virtual," but the infrastructure behind it is very physical: substations, transmission lines, gas plants, pipelines, and water. Duke's fuel costs include not only the fuel itself but the cost of transporting it, at the same moment our state is debating new gas generation and major pipelines. So we're asking the questions regulators should answer before these costs become embedded in people's bills: Who pays for the transmission upgrades and new generation? Who pays to transport the fuel? Who carries the risk if data center demand never materializes? And who bears the environmental and cultural costs when that infrastructure crosses rural, Black, and Indigenous communities? Rural families cannot become the subsidy for the AI economy. Read the full post: Are We Prepared? Community Pipeline Safety & Emergency Preparedness Meeting Wednesday, September 30 | 6:00–8:00 PM EDT 5th & Washington, 103 S Fifth St, Mebane, NC | Join in person If a pipeline emergency happened tomorrow, would you know what to do? Would you even know there was an emergency? Who would warn you? 7 Directions of Service invites residents living near pipeline infrastructure in North Carolina and Virginia to an interactive community meeting on pipeline safety and emergency preparedness. Together, we'll: Learn how pipeline emergencies are detected and communicated Walk through a hypothetical emergency scenario Ask what the plan is for elders, children, people with disabilities, and families without transportation or reliable cell service You don't need to be a pipeline expert. Your questions and experiences will help shape community recommendations for pipeline operators, emergency officials, and regulators. Are we prepared? Join us and help find out. Volunteers Needed: Community Pipeline Watch Three major natural gas projects, the Southeast Supply Enhancement Project (SSEP) , MVP Southgate , and the T-15 Reliability Project , are moving through communities across North Carolina. 7 Directions of Service is expanding our community-led construction, water, and air monitoring, and we need you. Permits have requirements. Construction has conditions. Environmental protections only work when someone is paying attention to whether they are being followed. That's where community monitoring comes in. You don't have to be a scientist, attorney, or environmental professional. Training and guidance will be provided. Choose the area that fits you: Construction Watch: Observe construction from lawful public locations and document erosion, sediment, or stormwater concerns Water Watch: Monitor streams, creeks, and wetlands near construction areas Air Watch: Help with community air monitoring and maintain equipment Research & Compliance: Review public NCDEQ and FERC records for inspections, incidents, and enforcement Mapping & Data: Organize photos, locations, and records to spot patterns across all three projects Community Outreach: Help residents learn how to document and report concerns Your safety comes first. Volunteers will never be asked to trespass, enter construction zones, confront workers, or put themselves in unsafe situations. Whether you can watch a creek near your home, review documents from your computer, or give a few hours a month, there is a place for you in this work. This is community science. This is environmental justice. This is protecting the places we call home. Ready to join? Help 7DS Rise to the Top: Give or Fundraise Through Earth Gives Wanted: 15 7DS Ambassadors We're looking for 15 people to become 7DS Ambassadors for the final week of Earth Gives, and we'd love for you to be one of them. As an Ambassador, you'll create your own free fundraising page for 7 Directions of Service and invite your circle to give: friends, family, coworkers, your congregation, your book club. It takes just a few minutes to set up, and Earth Gives provides step-by-step guidance and tools to help you share it. Why it matters: every person you bring in counts as a new donor, and the number of donors is exactly what helps small organizations like ours climb the leaderboard and compete for prize funds of $1,000 or more. If each of our 15 Ambassadors brings in just 5 donors, that's 75 new people standing with the frontlines. Ready to be one of the 15? Click "+ Fundraise" on . Watch & Learn Earth Gives is also hosting free Power Play sessions on the issues connected to our work: September 29: Using your voice as a climate force October 1: Climate is everyone's business October 5: Food, agriculture, and soil solutions Wear It Proud: Community Pipeline Watch T-Shirt We watch. We protect. We document. We act. Show the world where you stand. Wear your favorite 7DS gear to the next community meeting, public hearing, rally, or riverbank cleanup, and let people know that frontline communities are watching. Our Community Pipeline Watch Fundraiser T-Shirt ($40) is a soft, 100% cotton unisex tee available in multiple colors. Every purchase directly supports our Community Pipeline Watch program, funding: Monitor training Field equipment and water-monitoring supplies Mileage for volunteers tracking construction Documentation of environmental impacts On-site support for community members watching the pipeline When the pipeline companies say trust us, we say we'll be watching. Every shirt helps put another set of eyes on the ground. Already have 7DS gear? Snap a photo wearing it and tag us on social media. We'd love to see our community showing up! Dear Funders: Now Is Not the Time to Be Scared A few years ago, funders were showing up for frontline communities all across Turtle Island. Then Trump was elected, and almost immediately, funders panicked. We were even invited to an event where frontline leaders asked funders not to be afraid and to keep investing in the frontline. But as soon as the buffoons in charge started making threats, many of the people who felt uncomfortable pulled back. Some went across the pond to fund other fights. That left many frontline communities alone, without the resources to defend themselves. We don't have that option. Many of us work two and three jobs to make ends meet, and we still do what we have to do to protect our communities. We don't get the luxury of stopping and investing in something different. The pipeline is still coming. The water still needs protecting. Our families still live here. We are all in this together. We live on the same earth, breathe the same air, and drink the same water. What affects me will eventually affect you. So now is not the time to be scared. Now is the time to think outside the box and be courageous. Mini Mindfulness Retreat with the Thunderhorse Herd Saturday, October 24, 2026 | 1:00 PM When was the last time you gave yourself permission to simply slow down? Spend an intentional afternoon on the land with the Thunderhorse herd, away from phones, schedules, and the constant pressure to be doing something. This small-group retreat centers on stillness, nature, and reflection, with the calming presence of horses as part of the space. Horses naturally live in the present moment. Spending quiet time alongside them invites us to slow our own pace, notice what's around us, and reconnect with what gets lost when life gets busy. The afternoon may include: Guided mindfulness and breathwork Journaling and quiet time in nature Walking the land Gentle time with the horses Light refreshments You don't need to be a "horse person," and you don't need any meditation experience. Whether you're feeling busy, overwhelmed, or just ready for a quiet reset, this afternoon is for you. Just come as you are. | Space is limited. Saying "See You Soon" to Aidan and Kasey This month, we say see you soon to two members of our 7DS family. Aidan Loretz is stepping into a full-time role as Haw River Assembly's first-ever Environmental Justice Community Organizer. Aidan has been part of 7DS for years as a volunteer, intern, and team member, and has carried our values into every room: centering frontline voices, organizing across lines of difference, and standing up for the lands and waters we love. We are so proud to see Aidan bring that work to the Haw River full time, and we know our paths will keep crossing in the fights ahead. Kasey is following her joy, going full time with her comedy and satire performances. Kasey brought laughter, creativity, and heart to our team, and we can't wait to cheer her on from the audience. This isn't goodbye. It's a shift to new work and new relationships, and our circle only grows wider because of it. Thank you, Aidan and Kasey, for everything you've given to this community. A Note from Aidan "I want to say a huge thank you to Dr. Crystal Cavalier-Keck, Jason Crazy-Bear Campos-Keck, and my entire 7 Directions of Service team and greater community for years of support, training, love, and radical acceptance. I bring these values into my new role as Haw River Assembly's first-ever full-time Environmental Justice Community Organizer, and I will keep showing up in many of the same fights, from fracked-gas pipelines to data centers. Please reach out to mailto:aidan@hawriver.org if you'd like to discuss justice issues in the Haw River watershed or brainstorm how we can cause some good trouble together. This is not a goodbye to my 7DS community, just a shift to new capacity and relations." In solidarity, love, justice, and hope, Aidan Loretz, she/they Until Next Time This month reminded us that the biggest decisions about our land, our water, and our future are too often made in the dark, in rooms where frontline communities aren't invited. But it also reminded us of something stronger: when we show up together, in a theater in Chapel Hill, a room in New York, or a community meeting in Mebane, our voices carry. Thank you for reading, for showing up, and for standing with us. Whether you came to a screening, joined us online, made a call, or shared our work with a friend, you are part of this. Here's how to stay connected: Take action: Support the frontlines: Become one of our 15 Ambassadors and fundraise for 7DS Share this newsletter with someone who cares about their community Follow us** on social media for updates between newsletters We live on the same earth, breathe the same air, and drink the same water. What we protect, we protect for all of us, and for the generations still to come. Take care of yourselves, take care of each other, and we'll see you next month. | FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE MassGOP Research Department
The Dirty Dozen: 12 Times No Transparency Exposed Total Lack of Government Accountability
One-party government is the enemy of transparency. When one party holds the legislature, the corner office, and most local power for years, audits get delayed, records get withheld, and contracts start looking like a club. That is not left versus right. That is what happens when nobody in power has to answer to a real opposition.
Maura Healey, Senate President Karen Spilka, Speaker Ron Mariano and the Democrat Super Majority on Beacon Hill have ignored so many stories exposing corruption under their noses and have done nothing about it.
Any other state and just one of these instances would have caused outrage. But in Massachusetts, it is just another week, another scandal.
In November 2024, 72 percent of Massachusetts voters demanded an audit of the state legislature and made it the law. Two years later, it still has not happened.
The state has also refused to turn over SNAP and Medicaid records, while posting the highest SNAP error rate in New England. The Auditor has fought for the audit. Most of the political class has not.
Here are the Dirty Dozen times government has lacked accountability:

1. $2 billion in estimated rent over 40 years (up to 60 with options) on a Springfield courthouse awarded as a $600 million build-and-lease-back to a team tied to Conan Harris, husband of Rep. Ayanna Pressley, over experienced local contractors. Defended by Healey and Andrea Campbell
2. $1.75 billion, 35-year MassDOT highway-plaza contract awarded in 2025 to Ireland's Applegreen, a major donor to Governor Maura Healey, over Waltham-based Global Partners, whose bid was reportedly about $900 million lower than Applegreen's. The bid process was later found improper.
3. $4 billion economic-development bill signed by Governor Maura Healey in November 2024 included Section 269, granting BlueHub Capital retroactive-style immunity from consumer-protection claims after homeowners alleged the firm's "shared appreciation" mortgages took 40-60 percent of home appreciation. BlueHub's CEO is a longtime friend, donor, and fundraiser for Governor Maura Healey.
4. $250 million Boston housing award in 2024 from Mayor Wu's planning department to a Conan Harris-tied project--before the Springfield courthouse deal.
5. $7 million alleged SNAP store-reimbursement fraud: two Boston men charged in December 2025.
6. $1.6 million in COVID-era small-business loans Lawrence Mayor Brian DePeña was arrested in 2026 for allegedly diverting to personal and campaign expenses.
7. $1.4 million SNAP/MassHealth/disability fraud sweep: 15 people charged in June 2026.
8. $1.1 million alleged multistate SNAP/PUA identity-theft scheme: four people charged in February 2026.
9. $943,000 in losses from a related benefit-fraud crackdown: nine people charged in March 2026.
10. $36,000 State Rep. Christopher Flanagan was indicted in April 2025 for allegedly stealing from a Cape Cod trade association he ran, with additional charges in 2026.
11. $7,000 cash kickback Boston City Councilor Tania Fernandes Anderson took from a staffer's city-funded bonus in a City Hall bathroom. She pleaded guilty, resigned, and was sentenced.
12. LaMar Cook, deputy director of Governor Maura Healey's Western Massachusetts regional office, was arrested in October 2025 after state police intercepted cocaine shipments totaling 21 kilograms tied to deliveries at the Springfield State Office Building.

Why one-party rule hurts everyone. Without a real check, the majority has no incentive to open the books, enforce its own audit law, or explain why connected bidders beat local ones.
Corruption is not a partisan brand, but it grows in the dark with one party rule. Massachusetts does not need more loyalty tests. It needs records, competitive bidding, and officials who treat a voter-mandated audit as the law; not a suggestion.
###

body:
These reports tell a story.
#
Hi there,
**This Wednesday, the Federal Election Commission, the agency that enforces campaign finance laws, requires all federal campaigns to submit their campaign finance reports for the last time before Election Day this November.**
These deadlines are real, which is why, if your inbox is anything like ours, it’s probably filled with candidates trying to raise as much money as possible before their reports go public in a couple of weeks.
Those numbers will become reports that will tell a story about the strength of a campaign in fundraising—but they’ll also show where others are coming up short. And Republican Party committees, which entered this election cycle with a significant advantage over Democrats, will be ready to pounce, directing resources wherever they smell weakness—like a Democratic campaign that has raised less than its Republican opponent.
While Democrats have a great shot at flipping the House and Senate this November, recent polling shows many swing races will be extremely close.
**And a last-minute ad blitz backed by millions of dollars in GOP money could be enough to flip some of these important seats back in Republicans’ favor.**
That’s why, with one day left until the final FEC deadline before the election, we want to make sure the Democratic candidates in the most competitive races on our map have the resources they need to file strong campaign finance reports and fend off Republican attacks.
[**Consider donating $25, or whatever you can, to our Immediate Impact Fund today.**](https://act.swingleft.org/go/27?c0=immediate-impact-2026.DM5m6O&refcode=em20260929-2953&amount=25&t=2&akid=2953%2E1562180%2ERIOCyD)
**[Donate $25 Now](https://act.swingleft.org/go/27?c0=immediate-impact-2026.DM5m6O&refcode=em20260929-2953&amount=25&t=4&akid=2953%2E1562180%2ERIOCyD)**
The Immediate Impact Fund supports the Democratic candidates, state parties, and caucus committees that can benefit most from an immediate infusion of grassroots donations, and also supports Ground Truth, Swing Left’s volunteer-led organizing program that’s rebuilding trust in Democrats and making valuable insights available to Democratic campaigns and party committees.
It’s the highest-impact action you can take right now to make sure Democrats in the races that will decide the balance of power in Washington have the resources they need to win.
Thank you, as always, for everything you do.
— The Swing Left Team

**Since 2017, Swing Left has channeled the energy of grassroots volunteers and donors to elect Democrats, up and down the ballot, focusing on the most competitive races that can swing the national balance of power.** Right now, Swing Left is investing in grassroots organizing in key swing districts and initiatives across the country to flip the House and win the Senate and critical states in 2026. [**If you’d like to help support our work, you can make a donation using this link.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_sl_footer?refcode=em20260929-1&t=5&refcode2=2953_1562180_RIOCyD&akid=2953%2E1562180%2ERIOCyD)

| | Friends,
Over the weekend, Jason Colthorp at WDIV in Detroit moderated the first debate between my opponent and I for his Sunday show Flashpoint. The difference between Eli Savit and I couldn't be starker.
I have been a prosecutor for 30 years. I've locked up criminals and protected Eaton County's streets. I also started the first Economic Crimes Unit to go after fraudsters. I believe our next Attorney General needs to prioritize public safety and protect Michigan consumers.
My opponent, on the other hand, laid out a vision of more political activism from the Attorney General's office. I believe Michiganders are sick of lawfare after these last 8 years and want someone who will practice fair law instead.
[You can watch the entire debate here.](https://jrhsf9hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0011PGScCEMsMLuv9v45NB5GaxG2-Njiaa0bJZDjsUU6iq_eFrKW7WIt4c0wi8ojDlRRxjT3BBh-rmPI0bOjsApTe2peniRjIk2vM6_-pRcxWbaWWCZcpGRzkZ6geu717-X_3QLZKOW06it4BJcfKsVK10mI48eHch4bt3cJZcbE1poaiaaJlsbJQ==&c=jNDeWPyHMxXpA3R0FtLlrXnlaN99F0uy8uYmzxOAn1G4kzy6fWQvzg==&ch=HcysYA-b3xSozJCLW1CswlgPrs7PffgskDmRxyCxtFzlHxKw0L-GqA==)
As of right now, this is the only debate scheduled between my opponent and I. It's unfortunate as I think it was obvious to anyone who watched this one that Eli Savit would be an awful Attorney General and that I have the experience and leadership our state needs in that office.
Since there are no other debates scheduled, that means we need to make sure our ads reach the voters necessary to win this race.
[Will you donate today to help us ensure that?](https://jrhsf9hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0011PGScCEMsMLuv9v45NB5GaxG2-Njiaa0bJZDjsUU6iq_eFrKW7WIt4LaKhSQIhnHtjVwUvtYR6VrLBDrsIE2aCNs5YsHh7wVOOOeYbq861Z2t_eyhZVjbdRdE6UO3JRs0bzhTyjxLW5Klu66Fa_DPUve6Zsr6vxAl1hEtCHzZdRBOn1bJYHOK5UEsPPxdIUKrrUv-LJK2gegoq3Y3gb2F-d-p6Bf6pYP&c=jNDeWPyHMxXpA3R0FtLlrXnlaN99F0uy8uYmzxOAn1G4kzy6fWQvzg==&ch=HcysYA-b3xSozJCLW1CswlgPrs7PffgskDmRxyCxtFzlHxKw0L-GqA==)
I am honored to have the support of people like you in this race. You join Michigan law enforcement, businesses, and voters across the state who want public safety a priority in the Attorney General's office.
[Will you contribute to our campaign so we can win over more supporters in these last few weeks of this race?](https://jrhsf9hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0011PGScCEMsMLuv9v45NB5GaxG2-Njiaa0bJZDjsUU6iq_eFrKW7WIt4LaKhSQIhnHtjVwUvtYR6VrLBDrsIE2aCNs5YsHh7wVOOOeYbq861Z2t_eyhZVjbdRdE6UO3JRs0bzhTyjxLW5Klu66Fa_DPUve6Zsr6vxAl1hEtCHzZdRBOn1bJYHOK5UEsPPxdIUKrrUv-LJK2gegoq3Y3gb2F4SqzFHv2BT0&c=jNDeWPyHMxXpA3R0FtLlrXnlaN99F0uy8uYmzxOAn1G4kzy6fWQvzg==&ch=HcysYA-b3xSozJCLW1CswlgPrs7PffgskDmRxyCxtFzlHxKw0L-GqA==)

Doug Lloyd Eaton County Prosecutor Republican Nominee for Attorney General

clean_body: The difference between Eli Savit and I couldn’t be starker. | | | | | == | | | == | | Friends, Over the weekend, Jason Colthorp at WDIV in Detroit moderated the first debate between my opponent and I for his Sunday show Flashpoint. The difference between Eli Savit and I couldn't be starker. I have been a prosecutor for 30 years. I've locked up criminals and protected Eaton County's streets. I also started the first Economic Crimes Unit to go after fraudsters. I believe our next Attorney General needs to prioritize public safety and protect Michigan consumers. My opponent, on the other hand, laid out a vision of more political activism from the Attorney General's office. I believe Michiganders are sick of lawfare after these last 8 years and want someone who will practice fair law instead. == As of right now, this is the only debate scheduled between my opponent and I. It's unfortunate as I think it was obvious to anyone who watched this one that Eli Savit would be an awful Attorney General and that I have the experience and leadership our state needs in that office. Since there are no other debates scheduled, that means we need to make sure our ads reach the voters necessary to win this race. == I am honored to have the support of people like you in this race. You join Michigan law enforcement, businesses, and voters across the state who want public safety a priority in the Attorney General's office. == And please share this debate with your family, friends and networks. We have to get the word out. Recently, on the debate stage where Sarah came prepared for a lively debate about different ideas to make life better for Delawareans, her GOP opponent repeatedly disrespected her gender identity. He was eventually asked to leave the debate stage because of these petty tactics.
Sarah refuses to stoop to that level. She’s going to keep fighting tirelessly to lower costs for working families, but she needs your help to spread her positive message.
[**Make sure to read the email below if you haven’t already, and then pitch in $5, or any amount you can, to help Sarah win this November.**](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1184?c0=mcb-em-20260929-1.yqn7Ye&refcode=em20260929-3912&amount=5&t=2&akid=3912%2E21716%2EbzAuN2)

Team McBride

Date: Fri, Sept 18

Last night, I intended to debate my Republican opponent for the first time since I became the official Democratic nominee for Delaware’s at-large Congressional seat.
But what I’d hoped would be a spirited debate about the issues turned out to be something completely different:
**My opponent sought to disrespect me because of my gender identity.**
It wasn’t a slip-up. _He did it repeatedly — until organizers of the debate asked him to leave._
Let me be clear: I am not here to play their game. I won’t stoop to their level. And I refuse to let this nonsense distract from the real harm they’re trying to do at the expense of Delaware families.
Allowing a Republican to flip this seat means we’d have no chance at holding this administration accountable — and that’s an outcome I refuse to see happen. I treat every single day I serve in the halls of Congress as a privilege, and as an opportunity to do right by working Delawareans. I believe I owe that to the people who elected me in the first place, and there isn’t a day that goes by that I take your support for granted.
My vow to you is this: **petty politics like what occurred last night will never distract me from the work I signed up for.** I show up in Congress to deliver real results for Delawareans, not play performative politics for attention.

body:
AI data centers are popping up fast across the country. Tell us what you think about it.
#
Peter,
AI data centers are popping up _fast_ across the country, and one-third of them are either planned or already built in communities of color.
In states like Texas, data centers being built at rapid rates with little to no restrictions are driving people to vote for Democrats who will stand up to these tech corporations.
These massive tech facilities require enormous amounts of electricity and water to run. Across our communities, many families are raising serious concerns about what this will mean for rising monthly utility bills, water shortages, and local air quality.
Peter, we want to know where you stand on this issue.
**[Will you take a minute or two to take our survey and give us your thoughts on AI data centers?](https://act.votolatino.org/survey/em_ms_sur_ai_data_centers/?source=em20260929-628&t=1&akid=628%2E1366028%2E-qxyif)**

**Good Morning!** On this day in 1916, John D. Rockefeller was announced as [the world's first billionaire](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OqzAQRp8GOiNj8xMXLm4Kutxit0iJBnsIs2tsZI-C8var7Cts-Umfjo7O_TbfgALFx3_Y0fKa5ohnCciMeYYdMzkoAfIDCxdGDEeAyLOSahDSCGVmcExPnDuovV0RFeoabTsaOYyD7nS92UV3sHZSo5bgR7O00MpxgdarftX60tZk3zxplGml7Lu2ceAuq-8X02Ov1cVXnURPnHLzlSjyhmt4pSfmxqW9DnZjPkql_1VqqtR0nmezZGKIkRy8L5WaOHl4CYpio8Ipvyo1feLBuC-YhTLiI7lvXDEEzOKKLu1YxD3l4IuYKBcWVwqBUgTKWGfrj_O9yzBWnXzsQOFXhf9Y8GnVTwAAAP__tWOI5Q) due to his ownership of Standard Oil. His net worth equaled 2% of the nation's GDP that day. A 102-year-old in Ontario had one wish for her 100th birthday: to walk the new bridge from Windsor to Detroit. The bridge ran two years late, but [she walked it anyway](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGunDAQAL8GOiN7AXMULtJcd2lTooVdYCNjn8wGlL9_uvcLrx_NSPPnNb1QoqTtNx4cdM1T4vuMrMplwoOLLHhGLBufeipzfEdMOoEFb-xoYJxwUbl46rCmsDIDtzUHN4zWD77t2noPq7f9vBAB9H4gRw9yswfPPS1umLGrJXx8doTRWdt3rllweazUz2PPfQsPqjrLJJpL8zdL0p3X-D9fXJolH3UMu-r7rNpfFTwreN733WjBiyMmiiznv8IfsIJnEUWzcS4br6vZciFhs-ebjSTlklAlJ4xmLkIbGweu9TC0dQn0viVGOf1QdXY7UOJ3W3-47ArwFQAA__9WKINu), and turned down the walker. _Travel Tuesday_ has the rest. Could your pet be adding years to your life? A study that followed 3.4 million people for 12 years found that owners of a particular pet were 40% less likely to die during that period than those who didn't own it. **A Note from Cole, CEO of _The Flyover_** **Dear Reader,** Buried in the official editorial guidelines of one of the world's largest news organizations--on the books for decades, published for anyone to read--is a remarkable sentence. It says the word terrorist "can be a barrier rather than an aid to understanding." The written policy is that the plainest true word for an act of terror gets in the way of understanding it. That's not one outlet's quirk. It's mainstream media doctrine. And last month, you got to see where doctrine like that leads. Ahead of the 25th anniversary of September 11, reporters at another major news organization, a national public broadcaster, received a memo from the standards office: "Do not refer to the Sept. 11 attacks as terrorist attacks." The approved language for the deadliest terrorist attack in American history, in which nearly 3,000 people were murdered, was "hijackings that led to plane crashes." The memo leaked. Two days of daylight later, the broadcaster backed down. Sort of. They carved out an exception for 9/11, and only 9/11. The rule stands. And their defense was telling. They didn't argue that the rule is right. They argued that it's the industry standard and that newsrooms everywhere follow the same practice. The worst part is, they're right. It is the standard. That's the problem. You know why we exist. The truth isn't a barrier to understanding. It's the only road there. The facts arrive the way we found them, in plain words, and you decide what they mean. That's your job, and we'd never dream of doing it for you. We call things what they are. We keep the spin out and trust you with the facts. And _The Flyover_ stays free. A terrorist attack is a terrorist attack. We'd print that sentence any day of the week. No memo required. body:
Sarah has won tough races before. Let’s give her the resources to do it again.
#
I’ll get right to it, Peter:
Tomorrow is our last public end-of-quarter fundraising deadline before Election Day, and I’m asking you to help our endorsed candidate, Sarah Trone Garriott, finish strong.
Sarah is a minister, a working mom, and an Iowa state senator who put herself through college waiting tables and cleaning hotel rooms. She’s already won tough races — including defeating the Republican Senate president. Now she’s running to flip Iowa’s 3rd Congressional District.
**[With five weeks to go, will you split a donation between Sarah’s campaign and Small Town PAC before tomorrow’s deadline to help us put up strong public numbers and give her the resources to win?](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-20260929-stg.roVhvB&amount=5&refcode=em20260929-1153&t=1&akid=1153%2E34582%2EBzdBmx)**
Before Sarah ever ran for office, she supported survivors of domestic violence, served families as a hospital chaplain, and helped fight hunger in her community. When she saw Iowa’s elected leaders weren’t listening, she stepped up to serve in a new way.
**That’s the kind of experience we need in Washington. And Sarah has shown she can earn people’s trust across party lines: She won reelection in 2024 even as Trump carried her district.**
But I know from experience that these final weeks are tough. Republican super PACs are ramping up their attacks, and good candidates need the resources to get their own message in front of voters.
After tomorrow’s deadline, our fundraising numbers will be public. Republican operatives and megadonors will be looking to see whether we have what it takes to compete all the way through November. Let’s show them we do.
Small Town PAC needs to raise $60,000 by tomorrow night to help candidates like Sarah reach voters, answer attacks, and finish strong. We’ve backed them because we believe they can win. _Now we need to see it through._
**[Will you split $5 or whatever works for you between Sarah Trone Garriott and Small Town PAC before tomorrow night? Let’s help Sarah flip this seat, take back the House, and get to work for the communities counting on us.](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-20260929-stg.roVhvB&amount=5&refcode=em20260929-1153&t=2&akid=1153%2E34582%2EBzdBmx)**

I’m grateful,
Tim Walz

# Tuesday, September 29, 2026
---|---
**Good Morning!** On this day in 1785, three Comanche chiefs [rode into San Antonio](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLFuwyAQQL_G3mLhM8FiYKgqeUuXDh3RBc7hVGwsOCXp31fpL3R8y3vS-7r4C3Lm_faBGzl5rsXv9GiZRKj6Jlhb4qMShkSt1CtL2RtHDwrMSdkTWI9B-E5eYx_dVUU79uTG2Soz21lDnxxBUJMJpCYM0ziO2s56DVHPwRpQU-zZvXTKgh1HBaAGY7QJAOdznPXZrrrTiiJLqYMkEnpiW_NPuVMdQtn67JLI0brprYOlg4X24cHffFBkHEq9dbC8uIPlvWy4h0SnzwN3bskfhIG8VEJhan118XhwztzM3Gl125DzX0L-u-bu4DcAAP__iYN6Mw) alongside Pedro Vial and interpreter Francisco Xavier Chaves. Nearly three weeks of talks followed, and the two sides agreed to a peace treaty with Spanish Texas. Could your pet be adding years to your life? A study that followed 3.4 million people for 12 years found that owners of a particular pet were 40% less likely to die during that period than those who didn't own it. **A Note from Cole, CEO of _The Flyover_** **Dear Reader,** Buried in the official editorial guidelines of one of the world's largest news organizations—on the books for decades, published for anyone to read—is a remarkable sentence. It says the word terrorist "can be a barrier rather than an aid to understanding." The written policy is that the plainest true word for an act of terror gets in the way of understanding it. That's not one outlet's quirk. It's mainstream media doctrine. And last month, you got to see where doctrine like that leads. Ahead of the 25th anniversary of September 11, reporters at another major news organization, a national public broadcaster, received a memo from the standards office: "Do not refer to the Sept. 11 attacks as terrorist attacks." The approved language for the deadliest terrorist attack in American history, in which nearly 3,000 people were murdered, was "hijackings that led to plane crashes." The memo leaked. Two days of daylight later, the broadcaster backed down. Sort of. They carved out an exception for 9/11, and only 9/11. The rule stands. And their defense was telling. They didn't argue that the rule is right. They argued that it's the industry standard and that newsrooms everywhere follow the same practice. The worst part is, they're right. It is the standard. That's the problem. You know why we exist. The truth isn't a barrier to understanding. It's the only road there. The facts arrive the way we found them, in plain words, and you decide what they mean. That's your job, and we'd never dream of doing it for you. We call things what they are. We keep the spin out and trust you with the facts. And _The Flyover_ stays free. A terrorist attack is a terrorist attack. We'd print that sentence any day of the week. No memo required. So today I'm asking: if news that calls things what they are is something you want to see thrive, will you stand behind it? Support the news in plain words. Free, every morning. Greg Abbott for all 254 Texas counties Monday, clearing farmers and truckers to run dyed diesel in vehicles on public roads as pump prices hit a record $5.97 a gallon. Dyed diesel is the that powers tractors and bulldozers and is sold without the state motor-fuels tax. Texas normally bars it from public roads, and the proclamation lifts that ban and its penalties, though not the tax. Trucks hauling fuel, crops, or timber can also skip oversize and overweight permits and move loads . Abbott asked EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin to temporarily waive federal ultra-low sulfur diesel rules in 110 counties. "Texas agriculture and freight run on diesel ," Abbott said. "Record prices put both industries at risk and raise costs for every Texas family." Blue Cross Blue Shield of Texas is the , with more than 10 million members. | A Note from Cole, CEO of The Flyover Dear Reader, Buried in the official editorial guidelines of one of the world's largest news organizations—on the books for decades, published for anyone to read—is a remarkable sentence. It says the word terrorist "can be a barrier rather than an aid to understanding." The written policy is that the plainest true word for an act of terror gets in the way of understanding it. That's not one outlet's quirk. It's mainstream media doctrine. And last month, you got to see where doctrine like that leads. Ahead of the 25th anniversary of September 11, reporters at another major news organization, a national public broadcaster, received a memo from the standards office: "Do not refer to the Sept. 11 attacks as terrorist attacks." The approved language for the deadliest terrorist attack in American history, in which nearly 3,000 people were murdered, was "hijackings that led to plane crashes." The memo leaked. Two days of daylight later, the broadcaster backed down. Sort of. They carved out an exception for 9/11, and only 9/11. The rule stands. And their defense was telling. They didn't argue that the rule is right. They argued that it's the industry standard and that newsrooms everywhere follow the same practice. The worst part is, they're right. It is the standard. That's the problem. You know why we exist. The truth isn't a barrier to understanding. It's the only road there. The facts arrive the way we found them, in plain words, and you decide what they mean. That's your job, and we'd never dream of doing it for you. We call things what they are. We keep the spin out and trust you with the facts. And The Flyover stays free. A terrorist attack is a terrorist attack. We'd print that sentence any day of the week. No memo required. So today I'm asking: if news that calls things what they are is something you want to see thrive, will you stand behind it? Support the news in plain words. Free, every morning. **So far, we’ve raised about $12,500 toward our $100,000 goal.** We still have _a lot_ of ground to cover, and with just 35 days left until Election Day, we could really use your support right now. **[Rush a $5 or more contribution now to help us get there.](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260929_1_r2b.-tMiYq&refcode=em20260929-4075&amount=5&t=2&akid=4075%2E587540%2EzIndIQ)**
[****](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260929_1_r2b.-tMiYq&refcode=em20260929-4075&amount=5&t=3&akid=4075%2E587540%2EzIndIQ)
**Here’s what our fundraising gap really means:** it’s the difference between a candidate who can afford a full scale ground game, knocking on every door in their district, and one who can only send their team to knock half of them.
This money can make the biggest difference in the races that get the least attention: like many flippable U.S. House seats and especially races at the state legislature level. National media covers the Senate and Governors’ races around the clock, but state legislative races often have trouble getting the attention of even state or local media, which means many voters don't even know who's on the ballot. That gap shows up as down-ballot roll-off, and it's a chronic problem for Democrats in states across the country.
In one of Leaders We Deserve’s target red-to-blue races in Florida last cycle, we saw exactly how much down-ballot roll-off cost us. While Vice President Harris carried the district, thousands of Harris voters didn't vote all the way down the ballot and our endorsed candidate lost by just 485 votes. That's a margin clearly decided by roll-off.
This cycle, we're working to flip that same seat, and the polling shows it's within reach. But we need to ensure our candidate, Dr. Jane Aman, has the resources she needs to have enough canvassers knocking doors every day to get her message out to voters across the district. **And that’s just one example of how your donation to our Red-to-Blue Fund could power the next generation of bold, young Democrats to victory in November.**
We can’t afford to come up short in any of these critical races. **[If you can, please chip in $5, or whatever you can give today to help us close the gap. We’ve got some tough fights ahead, and your support will give our candidates the boost they need to flip state legislatures blue and take back Congress.](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260929_1_r2b.-tMiYq&refcode=em20260929-4075&amount=5&t=4&akid=4075%2E587540%2EzIndIQ)**

Thank you for your support.
— David Hogg
